newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Hong Kong tobacco exec appeals U.S. extradition.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Hong Kong tobacco exec appeals U.S. extradition.

text.p: Lawyers for a Hong Kong-based former British-American Tobacco Co executive argued in U.S. District Court on Monday their client should not be extradicted on bribery charges because he would face possible execution when the British colony returns to China on July 1.

Lui Kin-Hong, a former commercial director of British-American Tobacco Ltd in Hong Kong, is accused of accepting about $3 million in cash bribes and $1.5 million in unsecured loans to ensure the supply of cigarettes to a distributor.
Hong Kong has been seeking Lui's extradition since his December 1995 arrest at Boston's Logan Airport.

"The offenses he's charged with, cigarette smuggling -- this represents a loss of $1 billion to the (Chinese) government in tariff revenue. If they get their hands on him in China, he has a very good change of not only being imprisoned for a very long time, but he has a very good chance of being executed," Lui's lawyer, Harvey Silverglate, told U.S. District Judge Joseph Tauro.
But U.S. prosecutors countered in the Boston courtroom that the extradiction treaty between the United States and Hong Kong remained in effect.

"If he's going back to Hong Kong within 180 days, the British government is going to be competent to try and punish him. There is nothing in the text of the treaty that prohibits extradition prior to the reversion of Hong Kong," said prosecutor Michael Surgalla.
Another federal judge ordered Lui extradicted in August, but the former tobacco executive appealed that ruling.
Judge Tauro said he would have a decision on the extradiction before year's end.
